scope: Cross-runner APK reproducibility CI lane (two independent ubuntu-24.04 runners, pinned inputs, byte comparison) plus a same-machine signing-determinism experiment on the demonstrated reproducible APK. No app or asset changes; the lane is additive CI.

part_a_signing_determinism.purpose: Check that the packaging steps after the reproducible native build (zipalign + APK signing) are deterministic for the demonstrated APK.

input.path: /Users/cheng/apk-repro-ci/unsigned/buildA-unsigned.apk (derived from the demonstrated byte-identical buildA.apk, sha256 f8cc0b2f…)
input.apksigner_verify: DOES NOT VERIFY / missing META-INF/MANIFEST.MF (unsigned, as intended)

debug_key_signing.command: apksigner sign --ks ~/.android/debug.keystore --ks-pass pass:android --ks-key-alias androiddebugkey --key-pass pass:android --out debug-signed-N.apk <unsigned>

part_a_signing_determinism.older_scratch_runs: /Users/cheng/apk-repro-ci/out contains prior runs (zipalign pair identical 932bed…, re-sign pairs identical, test-key pair identical 8cd2931d…); the clean re-run above is the recorded result.
part_a_signing_determinism.conclusion: For this debug key and the demonstrated reproducible APK, zipalign and APK signing (v2, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5) are byte-deterministic in repeated runs.
limits: Debug signing only; release signing (different key/keystore, v3/v4 options) is not covered
Signing determinism says nothing about signing-security properties

design: Two independent, deliberately duplicated jobs (build-a, build-b) on separate runners perform the same clean pinned build (no Gradle/actions cache).

Pinned inputs: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792625234 (the epoch used by the demonstrated local experiment), BUILD_ID=vapor-repro via -PBUILD_ID, VERSION_CODE=1, Android SDK platforms/build-tools 35.0.0, NDK 27.3.13750724, cmake 3.22.1, Rust 1.99.0 with aarch64-linux-android, JDK 17 (temurin).
Each build removes app/build and app/.cxx first (the root-cause pass showed incremental packaging leaves history-dependent ZIP holes).
Each job records the APK sha256/size and uploads the APK + sha256 artifact.

A third compare job downloads both artifacts, verifies each recorded hash, compares sha256 and bytes with cmp, and fails on any difference; it prints diagnostics pointing at tools/tests/apk-repro-diff.py and the uploaded artifacts.
what_ci_must_prove: Both runners resolve the pinned toolchains
Both clean builds produce the same APK sha256, so the compare job passes and the job summary records PASS
If they differ, the compare job fails with both APKs available for byte-level diagnosis
residual_risks: Runner images can carry different patch-level JDK/build-tools metadata over time; the lane pins the package versions it can and treats any drift as a failure signal, not a silent pass
Gradle dependency resolution from remote repositories could change if a pinned dependency version is not immutable (the build already uses fixed versions, but no lockfile guarantee is added here)
Debug signing only; release signing and fully pristine caches are out of scope
part_b_ci_lane.status: First lane run executed: both builds succeeded, ZIP content identical, compare failed only on the per-runner debug signing block. Fixed CI debug keystore + automatic signing-block classification committed; second run pending.

ci_runs.diagnosis: The two independently built APKs are byte-identical in every ZIP entry (1638/1638, same order, same offsets, zero padding, zero differing CRC32). The only difference is the 4,096-byte APK signing block (sha256 source 77ba7a8f4fa859d0ed6ecea0a1b4c50eebfcd336d1f89d16948a00870ce11328 vs rebuild c01952130b8f074ebe98bbedb808e99f650f52cad26d2055620c4ab117fb41a8; 1,022 differing bytes): Android debug keystores are generated with a fresh random key on each runner, so signing differed while the build did not. tools/tests/apk-repro-diff.py (v1.1.0) was extended to detect and classify this signing-block-only case automatically.

ci_runs.fix: Commit the throwaway CI debug keystore .github/ci-debug.keystore and install it as $HOME/.android/debug.keystore in both jobs before the build, so both runners sign with the same debug key. The lane then tests build determinism rather than per-runner key generation. The result is recorded here after the workflow runs.

fixed_ci_keystore.type: JKS, RSA 2048, alias androiddebugkey, passwords android (public throwaway CI-only debug key, documented in .github/CI-DEBUG-KEYSTORE.md); never for releases
fixed_ci_keystore.rationale: Android debug signing uses a per-machine random keystore, which would make the signing block differ even for byte-identical builds; the first lane run proved exactly that.

limitations: CI lane proves same-image cross-runner reproducibility only; it does not prove reproducibility across different OS/toolchain versions
Signing experiment covers the debug key and v2 scheme on one host
No app code or packaging change
The fixed CI debug keystore is intentionally public and must never be used for releases; release-signing determinism remains untested.
